query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Reducing the spray distance to increase particle velocity will enable the HVAF-i7 torch to deposit a thicker FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy bond coat.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy particles with a 15–45 μm size distribution prepared as feedstock.
generation.intervention: Decrease the spray distance to increase the kinetic energy of the particles (i.e., increase particle velocity) during deposition.
generation.conditions: Deposition on substrates with internal diameters as small as 120 mm under elevated-temperature oxidation conditions typical for thermal-barrier applications.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced particle momentum upon impact leading to improved splat deformation and interlamellar bonding, which promotes thicker, more adherent coatings.
generation.mechanism: Higher particle velocity increases the kinetic energy transfer during impact, resulting in more effective flattening and bonding of particles, which, in turn, raises deposition efficiency and coating thickness while still minimizing as-sprayed oxidation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Under the modified condition (reduced spray distance), the HVAF-i7 system will yield a thicker, adherent bond coat compared to the baseline result achieved with the standard 15–45 μm feedstock and longer spray distances.
generation.baseline: Using the 15–45 μm feedstock with the HVAF-i7 torch at previous settings yields acceptable quality but inadequate thickness.
generation.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective as long as the reduction in spray distance does not cause adverse effects such as excessive substrate heating or overspray-induced coating defects. There is a limit below which further reduction may result in diminished coating uniformity or increased oxidation.
generation.uncertainty: The optimum reduction in spray distance (and corresponding increase in particle velocity) for the HVAF-i7 system has not been empirically established, and the relationship between spray distance, particle velocity, and deposition thickness may vary with system-specific parameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a controlled series of deposition experiments with the HVAF-i7 torch by systematically varying the spray distance (and consequently the particle velocity) while keeping the feedstock size distribution (15–45 μm) constant. Measure the coating thickness and assess coating integrity for each spray distance setting. The experiment should also check for the presence of unwanted oxidation or substrate damage.
measurements: Particle velocity measurements at different spray distances (e.g., using high-speed imaging or laser Doppler velocimetry).
Coating thickness (using cross-sectional microscopy or non-destructive thickness gauges).
Coating adhesion quality (via standardized adhesion testing).
Oxidation levels in the as-sprayed state and after high-temperature exposure.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If reducing the spray distance does not result in a statistically significant increase in coating thickness and/or introduces defects such as excessive oxidation or poor adhesion compared to the baseline condition, then the hypothesis that increased particle velocity (via reduced spray distance) effectively overcomes the thickness limitation will be falsified.
